recipes.name: Mom's Chocolate Chip Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.5 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a mixing bowl, cream butter and sugars. Add pudding mix, eggs and vanilla. Combine flour and baking soda; add to creamed mixture and mix well. Fold in chocolate chips.
Drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned.

review.reviewBody: I've used this recipe for years and everybody wants the recipe for it. I never give the recipe out because I've never seen a cookie recipe that calls for pudding before so I sort of consider it the secret ingredient of my signature cookie recipe. I always use Butter Flavor Crisco and a whole bag of chips. This recipe is easy to vary into peanut butter by using 1/2 c crisco and 1 c pb. You can make it into oatmeal cookies by using only 1 and 1/4 c of flour and 3 c of old fashioned oats. Or spice it up and use chocolate pudding and vanilla chips or peanut butter chips. Just have fun with this recipe. There are soooo many possibilities!!!

This is the only chocolate chip cookie recipe I use. My adult children request these whenever they come home. I started using chocolate pudding mix instead of vanilla and the cookies have a rich, chocolate flavor. I also form my cookies with a Pampered Chef, 2 TBS cookie scoop by placing one scoop on top of the other. Next, I press down a little bit with my palm and bake at 375 degrees for 15 minutes. The cookies are big and cake-like; they are not gooey. If you want more moisture, I suggest adding additional chips and using a little less flour.

AMAZING!!! Love these things. I added a little bit of salt and used Mexican vanilla (about 2 teaspoons). I also used chocolate chip and butterscotch chips. Added a little extra chips. I have always found when making these that you should roll dough into individual balls and place on a parchment paper lined sheet and stick in the freezer for at least an hr or two before cooking them. Enjoy. Anyone who doesn't enjoy this recipe clearly doesn't like chocolate chip cookies.
Wow!! Used 1c semi-sweet minis and 1c large milk choc chips. Also used a 1 1/2Tbsp scoop and they made the most yummy, super delicious cookies. Will definitely be our go to recipe from now on!

So good!! The best chocolate chip cookie recipe I have found yet - although I did substitute 1 cup of Crisco shortening, one bag milk chocolate chips, and added 1/2 tsp salt. Baked for 8 min at 350 degrees. I got about 40 cookies out of this batch. Thank you! note to self: next time, chill the dough overnight, and add 2 teaspoons cornstarch.

I love to cook, but I NOT a baker. My husband loves chocolate chip cookies, but I've never been able to master them. Decided to try this one for a cookie exchange and oh my gosh, they are amazing! I made a few tweaks and they are truly the most gorgeous cookies - crumbly on the outside, soft on the inside and they don't spread. This is what I changed - used butter flavor crisco instead of butter, 1 egg, 1 1/2 t. vanilla, 1/4 t. salt, lowered the flour to 2 cups, used chocolate chunks instead of regular. Baked at 350 for about 10-12 minutes. I also made them a little larger, rolled in balls and flattened just a tad on the top. Also, I doubled the recipe and used 1 box vanilla pudding & 1 box of cheesecake pudding. Everyone went crazy over these cookies and they all want the recipe! Gorgeous presentation and look better than gourmet cookie I've every seen. Can't say how happy I am to have found this recipe - I'm now a cookie master! Thanks for sharing!

I like to double the batch (except for the pudding mix) add 1 T crisco to prevent spreading, add 1 cup of blended oats and 4 oz milk chocolate shavings. I then freeze pre-scooped dough balls and put them into zipper bags. We have a dozen fresh baked cookies any time we want!

I love these cookies! I read the reviews and opted to melt the butter completely, leave out a 1 tbsp of pudding and add a 1/2 tsp of vanilla (I substitute our homemade maple syrup for vanilla) and these were crunchy on the edges and chewy in the middle..so good I had to put them up quick from the hubby so there would be some for tomorrow!! Will be keeping this recipe!

I made these cookies following Nilda Maria Williams. You melt the butter, add 2 + Tbsp milk leave out about a Tbsp of pudding add an extra 1/2 tsp vanilla. They turned out perfectly. So moist and fluffy. I baked these on parchment paper. I also measured the flour out by spooning the flour into the measuring the flour into the measuring cup so it's not so packed, and you get the right. Measurement of flour. I'm definitely making these again!!!

I used French vanilla pudding mix instead, and threw in some white chocolate chip cookies as well. To make it more aesthetically pleasing, I pushed in some chocolate chip cookies after the mixture too. Another tip: instead of dropping them as rounded, I rolled them into a ball with the palms of my hand and then pushed down on them a little ]
So chewy and good!! I did one cups of mini chocolate chips, 1/2 cup of toffee bits, and 1/2 cup of chopped cashews. They were perfect!
Ive been making these for years. People lose their minds. Eating other people's cookies makes me think about these cookies.
They were okay. I wouldn't make them again.
I typically make the 2x recipe and I've never had a complaint. I've also substituted in chocolate pudding mix - yum!
Love these cookies secret is not to let them cook to long
So good as is, but I like to add some grated orange zest to chocolate chip cookies which I think sends it over the top!
This is my favorite cookie recipe. I do not make any other chip recipe. You can change the flavor by changing the pudding mix. Nice and soft cookies.
I LOVE this recipe. The 2 changes I made was that I use Hershey Milk Chocolate chips and added a little extra vanilla flavoring. I'm just curious how well the dough freezes.....
So far in my chocolate chip cookie experience, this one takes the all time favorite!! Gobbled up by my adult kids and grandkids!! Talk about a keeper! And didn’t change a thing! Thank you!

6/16/2023 UPDATE; all these years later since I made the original review (2006) and this is STILL my favorite chocolate chip recipe. Everyone raves and always asks me how they bake up so nicely. These are along the lines of a 'softbatch' more than a chip ahoy. softer than crunchy. Love that. Original review: This is a great easy recipe..same as the Award Winning Choc. Chip Cookie, I think. I had a package of french vanilla. When I added it, I smelled that real fake 'coffee creamer vanilla' smell and was afraid it would be overpowering in the cookie. It also added a real dark yellow color to the batter. It did not overpower; as a matter of fact, I couldn't taste the vanilla really. They baked like a picture and baked 12 min. on the Airbake sheet, 10 minutes on the Oneida non-stick. Each cookie sheet holds alot, as they do not spread. They are cake-like in texture, real soft. Great for air mail travel which is where these are headed. I guess the debate will always continue: crisp or cakey. They tasted great. I used a package of those white chocolate/milk chocolate swirled chips and they looked pretty. I think the pudding more added to the texture and not to the taste. I would definitely make again especially if sending via airmail.
